findings.message: Read hook input from stdin. Claude Code supplies command-hook input through stdin, but the installed command passes no arguments. Consequently, this parses `{}` and exits at the tool-name check, allowing every shutdown. Read stdin and test the hook using the installed invocation rather than passing JSON as an argument.

Inspect the actual SendMessage shutdown fields. SendMessage shutdown requests use top-level tool-input fields `type: "shutdown_request"`, `recipient`, and `content`, rather than `message.type` and `to`. Even after fixing input transport, actual shutdown requests exit here because `message` is absent. Inspect the real tool schema and use representative payloads in the tests.

Match the sidecar format produced by the review workflow. The existing review gate locates sidecars named `${agent}--${contentHash}.json`, not filenames containing the branch. A normally completed review therefore fails this check and leaves the implementer blocked once shutdown interception works. Read and validate sidecar metadata against the relevant branch instead of requiring a branch substring in the filename.
